results.summary: This project is an 8-bit comparator that compares two input values and indicates whether they are equal, greater, or less than each other. It is implemented as a purely combinational circuit in Verilog, requiring no clock or sequential logic. The inputs can be driven by switches or FPGA pins, and the output is presented on the output pins. The design can be verified through simulation or on Tiny Tapeout hardware.

This project is a PWM generator with timer and counter functionality, designed for power management applications. It uses GPIO pins for input and output, and includes a clock divider to generate the PWM signal. The design is intended for educational purposes and can be tested with a simple testbench. External hardware such as LEDs or motors can be connected to observe the PWM output.

This project is a video and graphics generator that outputs a continuous pixel stream for display. It is verified using a cocotb-based Python testbench that reconstructs full images from the output. The design includes logic gates and counters to generate the video signal. It can be connected to a VGA or other display interface for visual output.

This project is a simple counter demo implemented on a RISC-V CPU, with output displayed on a 7-segment display. It is designed for educational purposes to demonstrate basic CPU and counter operation. The counter increments and the value is shown on the 7-segment display. The design can be tested using simulation or on Tiny Tapeout hardware.

This project is a music synthesizer that generates audio tones using an LFSR-based noise source and an NCO for pitch control. It outputs audio through a PWM or DAC interface. The design includes a synthesizer core and can be used for chiptune-style music generation. External speakers or audio amplifiers can be connected to the output.

This tile combines a byte adder, an 8x8 multiplier, and a reciprocal-ROM divider behind a small register-loaded interface with four task slots and command, mode, and bank selection pins. It is verified with a cocotb testbench and implemented as an ASIC. The design supports basic arithmetic operations and can be used for educational or computational purposes.

This project is a UART-based pattern generator that uses an LFSR and counter to produce test patterns. It is designed for factory testing and communication applications. The design includes a UART interface for external communication. It can be used to generate deterministic patterns for testing other hardware.

This project is a simplified ECC accelerator implemented in Verilog for ASIC implementation. It performs error correction using cryptographic algorithms. The design includes an ALU, multiplier, and register file to support the computation. It can be tested through simulation or on Tiny Tapeout demonstration boards.

This project is an ECC accelerator that performs error correction using cryptographic algorithms. It includes an ALU, multiplier, and register file for computation. The design can be tested entirely using Tiny Tapeout simulation, gate-level simulation, or FPGA-based verification environments. It is intended for hardware acceleration of error correction tasks.

This project is an ECC accelerator with error correction capabilities, implemented with an ALU, multiplier, and register file. The documentation is brief and reports no silicon results. It can be tested using simulation or FPGA-based verification. The design is intended for hardware acceleration of error correction tasks.
